text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Serbian parliament elects Vlajko Stojiljkovic, current President of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce, as new Serbian Interior Minister and Deputy Prime Minister.
- Serbian parliament passes 1996 final budget statement at 10.24 billion dinars or 85.4 percent of the plan.

- Serbs in Eastern Slavonia say they lost about 10,000 votes because of residents who did not obtain Croatian documents in time for the polls. They say the international community will decide on regularity of the polls.

- Bosnian Serb chief of general staff General Pero Colic describes security situation in Bosnian Serb republic as unfavourable because Bosnian Croats and Moslems have not abandoned their intention to change borders.
- All Belgrade city services are ready for the tenth Belgrade Stark marathon which will be held on April 19.
NASA BORBA

- Leadership of the ruling Democratic Party of Montenegro reaches compromise over the dispute with Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic according to which the Prime minister agrees to make a major cabinet reshuffle within a month and a half.
- Montenegrin Public prosecutor clears work of state security service of suspicion after a probe requested by Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic.
- Chief international negotiator for the succession of ex-Yugoslavia Sir Arthur Watts expected to visit former Yugoslav republics at the end of April to present final draft of his proposal.
- Belgrade-based Jugoexport to open a store with Versace production programme in Belgrade by end of April.

- Programme of revitalisation and transformation of Zastava cars comprises active participation of the state so that its privatisation will go according to a special programme of the republican government.
- Yugoslavia's industrial output up 7.4 percent in March on February and 9.2 percent on same month last year, statistics office says.
- Yugoslav government to launch 200 million dinars worth of three-month bonds on the Belgrade and Montenegro bourses on April 22. Bonds carry a 4.5 percent monthly interest.
- U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata arriving in Belgrade Wednesday evening within a tour of former Yugoslav countries.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Reconstruction of Belgrade-Bar railway line begins, first section Podgorica-Biocep to be completed by end of May.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Federal government approves lower tax rates of 10 percent instead of 20 percent for purchase of taxi, and rent-a-car vehicles.
- Germany's Krupp concludes four million mark deal on delivery of spare parts for Yugoslav power industry to be paid with exports of parts made by the Yugoslav metal industry.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT to introduce direct flights to Ohrid, Corfu, Rhodes, Palma de Mallorca, Ismir and Tunisia during the summer season.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA

- "Following detailed probe into the state security service (requested by Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic on April 11) I have assesssed there have been no illegalities in the work of the service and there are no grounds for launching a procedure of determining responsiblity of any of its employees", says Montenegrin public prosecutor Vladimir Susovic.
- Montenegro's March industrial output is 10.2 percent up on February, trade deficit in the first three months of the year is $58 million, according to republican statistics office.
- Montenegro does not have funds to pay imports of seven million KWh of electricity a day and will have to introduce power cuts if there is no rain.
- Montenegro's tourism trade union demands abolishment of visas for foreign tourists, demand supported by Montenegrin tourism ministry. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
